details: CONFIRMED, reproduced. Before the change the hook was the only writer, so dropping marks of HEAD on its own failure was
safe: any mark there predated this checker. Now the command commits a mark during the checker's run, and the failure path
(wt from the Worktree: label, stale_commits = HEAD plus the newest marked ancestor with only inert files after it) treats
that fresh mark as stale. This is exactly the train-8 prompt shape (Report label = an old findings file), so the change's
promise "relay check show never shows an older mark as current after a newer record" fails on the live case it was
written for. The fixer saw it ("Open risk ... left unchanged"); a HIGH inside the change is fixed before the merge.
Size: 30 minutes.
evidence: (RecordMakesMark subclass; transcript with the label above; old file utime -3600 s):
hook: check mark not written for wt/train-1: the check data is older than the checker's start
verdict: no check of wt/train-1 covers lib/shared.py, which the ready changes it holds changed together or which it rewrote; run relay gate, then delegate:checker
failing_case: Train worktree (two riders both changed lib/shared.py), gate green. Checker prompt: "Check: <old>.json ... Worktree: <train>.
... Report: <old>.json." where <old>.json is older than the checker's start (the train-8 prompt shape). The checker runs
`relay check record check --input` with report = another path: the command commits "relay: check of H" (show: "mark H: open 0").
Then the SubagentStop hook runs: "check mark not written for wt/train-1: the check data is older than the checker's start",
and stale_commits() returns [mark commit, H] (only inert files after H), so drop(H) removes the mark. Now: show lists the
riders' older mark as current and the merge hook refuses ("no check of wt/train-1 covers lib/shared.py"). Expected: the
command's mark of H stays; the hook reports its own failure without removing a mark it did not write for this record.
fix_hint: In the failure path, do not drop a mark committed after the checker's start (the mark's "time", or its commit date, at or
after `start`): it is this checker's own record. Add the scratch case as a test in tests/test_check_mark_on_record.py.
pass_cases: 1. The failing case above: after the hook, `relay_marks.show(main, "wt/train-1")` still lists "mark H: open 0" and the merge hook's verdict for wt/train-1 is None.

2. A re-check with a correct Report: label whose record is open 1 at the same head H that held an open 0 mark: the mark of H is replaced with open 1 (a stale clean mark never outlives a failed re-check, design 6.5).
3. A checker whose label file is missing and that recorded nothing, on a HEAD with an old clean mark of HEAD: that stale mark is still removed (today's behaviour).
4. Label correct, command already made the same mark: the hook adds no commit (tests/test_check_mark_on_record.py test 2 keeps passing).
reason: tests/test_check_mark_hook.py:89 and :110 pass; the hook has no drop path; both fail at 4762d51. Pass-case 3 (stale clean mark removed) dropped by the front's decision that the hook never removes a mark.
findings.summary: when the hook cannot use its Report: label it drops the mark the command just committed, so show and the merge fall back to an older mark

details: CONFIRMED by reading. docs/plans/review-gate.md section 6: "the checker writes only its report; a SubagentStop hook copies
its verdict into a committed mark; no model writes a mark", and step 1: "Does nothing unless agent_type is exactly
delegate:checker". Section 9's guard keeps agents from writing .relay/checks by hand; no guard limits who runs
`relay check record check` (grep of plugins/core/hooks: only check-mark.py names it). The change makes the mark a side
effect of a command any session can run, so the independence of the check (the one review plus a separate checker) is no
longer enforced by code. The queue item's pass case ("the same record makes a relay: check of <head> commit") cannot be
met inside section 6, hence a design finding.
Design: whether `relay check record check` (any caller) may commit a mark, or marks stay hook-only for delegate:checker
(then the hook finds the record the checker actually wrote, e.g. from the "recorded <path>" line of its own transcript,
instead of trusting only the prompt's Report: label).
Size: 30 minutes either way, after the owner's word.
evidence: docs/plans/review-gate.md:316-325 (section 6, steps 1 and 5); bin/relay:578 calls relay_marks.write_check_mark with no
agent or has_relay check; grep -rln "check record" plugins/core/hooks -> only check-mark.py.
failing_case: A worker or fixer in wt/x (project with .relay/) writes a check TOML with every finding MET and runs
`relay check record check --input it.toml`. Now: "recorded ... (open 0, queued 0); check mark committed", a commit
"relay: check of <head>" with open 0, and with a green gate the merge hook lets wt/x into master with no checker ever run.
Before the change: the record existed but no mark (the hook fires only for agent_type delegate:checker), and the merge
was refused "no check mark for wt/x".
fix_hint: Owner choice. Keeping the design: revert the command's mark; in the hook take the record path from the last
"recorded <path> (open" line in the checker's transcript, falling back to the Report: label.
pass_cases: 1. Artifact: docs/plans/review-gate.md section 6 states who may cause a mark: either it keeps "Does nothing unless agent_type is exactly delegate:checker" and the command makes no mark, or it is amended to say the command makes it for any caller, with the owner's word.
2. If the design stays: a record by a non-checker agent leaves no mark and the merge hook refuses wt/x "no check mark".
3. If the design stays: the queue item's train case recorded by a delegate:checker leaves the mark (via the hook, also when the Report: label names another file).
reason: bin/relay equals master (command makes no mark); tests/test_check_mark_hook.py:79 passes (worker gets no mark, merge refuses); fails at 4762d51. Marks stay hook-only for delegate:checker, per the front's decision (owner can reverse).
findings.summary: any agent that runs relay check record check now gets a mark the merge trusts; the design makes marks only from a delegate:checker via the hook

details: CONFIRMED from the transcript (agent-a0bc62598ac915d8a.jsonl): the only record-like call is none; check3-train-8.json is
dated 18:56 local, an hour after this checker (14:55Z), i.e. the second checker's. The brief asks for the cause (principle
6); the change fixes a different path (record by command) and leaves this one. The hook's design says it "always exits 0
(it never blocks)", so making the checker continue needs that decision changed.
Design: the check-mark hook may block a delegate:checker's stop once when no valid record newer than its start exists.
Size: 30 minutes.
evidence: Tool calls: relay check findings, relay check show check2, pytest in base3, then StructuredOutput {"open": 0, ... "summary": "Report: .../check3-train-8.json ..."}.
ls -la reports: check3-train-8.json Oct 25 18:56; check2-train-8.json Oct 25 19:27.
failing_case: Train-8, 25 Oct: prompt "Check: check2-train-8.json ... Report: check2-train-8.json"; the checker ran relay check findings,
the tests, then StructuredOutput with "open 0" and never ran relay check record check. With this change the same run still
leaves no record and no mark; the hook says "the check data is older than the checker's start" in a systemMessage the
workflow does not surface; show keeps 3e4a0a5 (open 1) and the front believes open 0. Expected: the checker is stopped
and told to record (or the front is told plainly that no check was recorded).
fix_hint: Owner choice on blocking; cheapest without it: the delegate skill / workflow prompt names a new Report path per check and
the hook refuses a Report label equal to a Check: file with a plain message.
pass_cases: 1. A delegate:checker whose transcript holds no successful `relay check record check` and whose label file is older than its start: it is not allowed to finish silently (SubagentStop blocks once with "run relay check record check --input <toml>", or the reply the front reads says "no check recorded").
2. A checker that did record (label right): finishes with no block and the mark is made.
3. Artifact: the delegate skill's check prompt never gives a Report: path equal to a Check: findings file (or the hook refuses that prompt with a message saying so).
reason: tests/test_check_mark_hook.py:123 passes: a checker with no record gets exit 2 once (stop_hook_active ends it); fails at 4762d51.
findings.summary: the train-8 cause is untouched: a checker that ends without recording leaves the old mark and only a systemMessage nobody in a workflow sees

details: CONFIRMED by reading: cmd_check_record calls relay_marks.write_check_mark(data["worktree"], data) unconditionally;
write_check_mark -> put() writes FOLDER files and commits them. The hook guards this with `if not relay_git.has_relay(cwd):
return None`; the shared code lost that guard on the command path. Reachable on ordinary use in every non-relay project
that records checks; the owner just said the arsenal probe may run in parallel with this relay work.
Size: 5 minutes.
evidence: bin/relay:577-581 (no has_relay); plugins/core/hooks/check-mark.py:174-175 (`if not relay_git.has_relay(cwd): return None`);
failing_case: A project whose default branch has no .relay/ (the check record is still used there, e.g. a Glonass repo or arsenal before
its probe): a checker runs `relay check record check --input c.toml` with worktree = its task worktree. Now: a commit
"relay: check of <head>" adding .relay/checks/<head>.json and <head>.check.json lands on the task branch and goes into its
merge request. Before: nothing was committed (the hook does nothing unless relay_git.has_relay). Expected: no commit; the
record is written and the command prints "recorded <path> (open n, queued m)".
fix_hint: Call write_check_mark only when relay_git.has_relay(worktree); print "; check mark committed" only then. Add a test with a repo whose master has no .relay/.
pass_cases: 1. Repo without .relay/ on its default branch: record check exits 0, prints "recorded", git log of the worktree is unchanged, no .relay/ folder appears.
2. Repo with .relay/: the queue item's train case still makes the mark (tests/test_check_mark_on_record.py test 1).
reason: Resolved by undoing the command's mark: bin/relay equals master, so no .relay/checks commit in a project without .relay/ (the hook returns early without has_relay).
findings.summary: in a project without .relay/ the command now commits .relay/checks files into the task branch

details: CONFIRMED by reading write_check_mark's early return. Misleading only; Size: 5 minutes.
failing_case: Run `relay check record check --input same.toml` twice for the same head and findings: the second run prints
"; check mark committed" though no commit was made (write_check_mark returned early).
fix_hint: Have write_check_mark return whether it committed, and print accordingly.
pass_cases: 1. First run: "check mark committed" and one new commit.
2. Second identical run: no new commit and the message says the mark was already there (or says nothing about a commit).
reason: Resolved by undoing the command's mark: the "check mark committed" message is gone with it.
findings.summary: the command says check mark committed when write_check_mark found the same mark and committed nothing
